part.text:
All 31 tests pass. The implementation in `bowling.py`:

- **`roll(pins)`** — validates the pin count (0–10), rejects rolls after the game is complete, and routes to normal-frame or tenth-frame logic. Normal frames close on a strike (1 roll) or a second roll that doesn't exceed the remaining pins. The tenth frame allows up to 3 rolls, with the constraint that the second bonus roll can't be a strike unless the first one was, and can't exceed the remaining pins after a non-strike first bonus roll.
- **`score()`** — raises unless all 10 frames are complete (including any tenth-frame bonus rolls). It flattens the frames into a roll list and walks frames with a running roll offset, applying strike/spare bonuses (next two / next one roll) — the offset approach correctly handles variable-length frames.

Two bugs surfaced during testing and were fixed: a tenth-frame spare was being marked complete after 2 rolls (before its bonus roll), and the scorer originally indexed the flat roll list by frame number instead of by cumulative roll offset.
